name: Traxler Counter-Attack — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Traxler Counter-Attack. Find the winning 2-move sequence to consolidate and win material against Black's sacrificial attack.

drills.name: King to d3, Attack the Knight
drills.description: After 6...Nxe4+, White's king is on f2. Find the best way to step out of check and consolidate the center.
drills.briefExplanation: King steps up to e3 to attack the knight, followed by d3 and Qf3 to consolidate White's extra material.
drills.explanation: 7.Ke3! d3 attacks the e4-knight. This is a key defensive resource in the Traxler. Follow up with Qf3 to consolidate the extra material.

drills.name: Defensive Queen Check
drills.description: Black's queen is on h4. White needs to defend the king and capture the loose knight on e4.
drills.briefExplanation: Qf3 defends the king and attacks e4. After capturing on e4, c3 prepares to drive away the knight and solidify.
drills.explanation: 8.Qf3! defends the king and attacks the e4 knight. If Black takes on e4, White has gained time and material while the king finds safety.

drills.name: Strike in the Center
drills.description: White is under pressure. Use a central pawn break to open lines and activate pieces.
drills.briefExplanation: d4 opens the center. After dxc5, Qf3 defends the king and prepares to consolidate the material advantage.
drills.explanation: 8.d4! challenges the center and opens the d-file and diagonals. This is a classic way for White to fight back in the Traxler chaos.

drills.name: Pin the Queen
drills.description: Black's queen is active on f6. Find the strong pin that wins the queen and simplifies the game.
drills.briefExplanation: Bg5 pins and wins the queen. After Bxf6, Nc3 develops the last piece to finalize the win.
drills.explanation: 11.Bg5! pins the queen to the king (or creates devastating threats). Black is forced to give up the queen or suffer decisive material loss after Bxf6.
